75
Ewr Hochfürstliche Durchlaucht
Tage ich die mir höchſt gnädigſte Comunicirte
Schreiben d. Gr. v. S. unterthänigst wieder
zu Füßen —
Es freut mich daß der Gr. ſich bey der
ganzen Sache so gerade beträgt, und
am Ende seinen Vorteil einsicht —
Nur traure ich auf der andern Seite
aber zu sehr, daß ich in dieser Sache
abermals einen der Menschheit entehrende
zug erfahren müßen, und dan daß mir
die Gelegenheit benommen wird Ewr.
Hochfürstliche Durchlaucht einen recht reelen
Dienst zu leisten und Höchst Ihnen so ein
40 bis 50/m Rthl zu gewinnen —
Aus Bonn schreibt Reinhardt daß
wegen der Assistenz des Fisci noch nichts erfolgt
ist — Gott! wie bedaurens werth sind die Menschl
deren Worte man ein Glauben beimeßen darff,
Von dH. v Goldbeck aus Berlin habe ich gestern
ein Schreiben erhalten, worin der sagt
"Bis hieher habe wegen das Südpreußischen
Departement in der Residenz viele Gerüchte
rouliert. Vor ein paar Tage aber habe
ich von einen zuverläßigen Manne gehört
daß es dH. Gr v. Hoym behält."
Er schreibt die Majestät hätten ihm zu seinen sonst sehr
ausgedehnten Justiz Departement um auch noch die
Anabach in Baerautschen Provinzen zugeben und
befohlen — Einige Neuere Gesetze zu entwerfen.
Der Himmel weis was an den allen ist
Den vor etwa 3 Tagen ist ein Vertrauter des
Minister Haugwitz ein gewißer Priebich hierdurch
gegangen, dieser hatt den Rath Kruger fest
versichert, daß der Minister Haugwitz Sudpreußisch
Minister wäre —
Chełmski hatt noch nicht apellirt und vieleicht
können die Güter auch schon auf Johanni ohne Anstoß
mit verpachtet würden
Melzer ist wie der retournirte Expresse die Nach¬
richt von Gravenitz bringt nicht zu Hause gewesen
kömt aber in 2 Tage wieder um da wird das
formular zur Vollmacht als auch die sonstigen
Berichte erfolgen
In tiefsten Respect beharre
Ewr Hochfürstliche Durchlaucht
Breslau den 1ten April
1798.
treu unterthänigster Knecht
v Triebenfeld

translation.en: 75 Your Most Serene Highness, I [uncertain: Tage] most humbly lay again at your feet the letters of the Count von S. most graciously communicated to me — It gladdens me that the Count conducts himself so straightforwardly in the whole affair, and in the end perceives his own advantage — Only, on the other hand, I grieve all too much that in this matter I have once again had to experience a trait dishonouring to humanity, and then that the opportunity is taken from me of rendering Your Most Serene Highness a truly substantial service and of gaining for you, Most High, some 40 to 50/m Rthl — From Bonn Reinhardt writes that

nothing has yet followed concerning the assistance of the fiscal authority — God! how pitiable are the [uncertain: Menschl] whose words one may set any belief in. From Mr von Goldbeck in Berlin I received a letter yesterday, in which he says: "Up to now many rumours have been current in the Residence concerning the South Prussian Department. A few days ago, however, I heard from a reliable man that Count von Hoym is keeping it." He writes that His Majesty had been pleased to add to his otherwise already very extensive Justice Department the [uncertain: Anabach in Baerautschen] provinces as well, and had commanded — that some newer laws be drafted. Heaven knows what there is in all this; for about 3 days ago a confidant of Minister Haugwitz, a certain Priebich, passed through here, and he firmly assured

the councillor Kruger that Minister Haugwitz was to be South Prussian minister — Chełmski has not yet appealed, and perhaps the estates may also be leased out along with the rest at Midsummer without obstruction. Melzer, when the returning express brought the news from Gravenitz, was not at home, but comes back in 2 days, [uncertain: um] and then the form for the power of attorney will follow, as will the other reports. In deepest reverence I remain, Your Most Serene Highness's Wrocław, the 1st of April 1798.

most faithful and humble servant v Triebenfeld

75 Your Most Serene Highness, I [uncertain: Tage] most humbly lay again at your feet the letters of the Count von S. most graciously communicated to me — It gladdens me that the Count conducts himself so straightforwardly in the whole affair, and in the end perceives his own advantage — Only, on the other hand, I grieve all too much that in this matter I have once again had to experience a trait dishonouring to humanity, and then that the opportunity is taken from me of rendering Your Most Serene Highness a truly substantial service and of gaining for you, Most High, some 40 to 50/m Rthl — From Bonn Reinhardt writes that

nothing has yet followed concerning the assistance of the fiscal authority — God! how pitiable are the [uncertain: Menschl] whose words one may set any belief in. From Mr von Goldbeck in Berlin I received a letter yesterday, in which he says: "Up to now many rumours have been current in the Residence concerning the South Prussian Department. A few days ago, however, I heard from a reliable man that Count von Hoym is keeping it." He writes that His Majesty had been pleased to add to his otherwise already very extensive Justice Department the [uncertain: Anabach in Baerautschen] provinces as well, and had commanded — that some newer laws be drafted. Heaven knows what there is in all this; for about 3 days ago a confidant of Minister Haugwitz, a certain Priebich, passed through here, and he firmly assured

the councillor Kruger that Minister Haugwitz was to be South Prussian minister — Chełmski has not yet appealed, and perhaps the estates may also be leased out along with the rest at Midsummer without obstruction. Melzer, when the returning express brought the news from Gravenitz, was not at home, but comes back in 2 days, [uncertain: um] and then the form for the power of attorney will follow, as will the other reports. In deepest reverence I remain, Your Most Serene Highness's Wrocław, the 1st of April 1798.

most faithful and humble servant v Triebenfeld
summary_en: Triebenfeld returns the letters of Count v. S. that were sent to him. He is glad the Count is behaving honestly, but regrets that he cannot win the Prince 40 to 50/m Rthl. According to Reinhardt, nothing has come of the matter of the assistance of the Treasury. Goldbeck hears that Hoym is keeping the South Prussian Department; Priebich, on the other hand, assured Councillor Kruger that Haugwitz would become minister. Chelmski has not appealed, and the estates might perhaps be leased out at Midsummer. The form for the power of attorney will follow after Melzer's return.
summary_de: Triebenfeld schickt die ihm mitgeteilten Schreiben des Gr. v. S. zurück. Er freut sich, dass der Graf sich gerade verhält, bedauert aber, dem Fürsten nicht 40 bis 50/m Rthl gewinnen zu können. Laut Reinhardt ist wegen der Assistenz des Fisci nichts erfolgt. Goldbeck hört, Hoym behalte das Südpreußische Departement; Priebich versicherte Rath Kruger dagegen, Haugwitz werde Minister. Chełmski hat nicht appelliert, die Güter könnten vielleicht zu Johanni verpachtet werden. Das Formular zur Vollmacht folgt nach Melzers Rückkehr.

reading.notes: Triebenfeld in Breslau writes to the Prince. He returns the letters of a "Gr. v. S." that the Prince had passed to him. He regrets losing the chance to gain the Prince 40 bis 50/m Rthl. Reinhardt writes from Bonn: nothing yet on the Assistenz des Fisci. Goldbeck reports a Berlin rumour that Hoym keeps the Südpreußisches Departement. Priebich, a confidant of Haugwitz, told Rath Kruger that Haugwitz will become minister. Chełmski has not appealed, so the estates may be leased at Johanni. Melzer was away when the express came back with news from Gravenitz; the form for the power of attorney will follow. Nothing on Trąbczyn.
